# SOP-P3-L2-05 Planned shutdown - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, EQ-P3-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-044, MM-P3-L2-SB01, SB-1015

Purpose
1. Define the controlled planned shutdown sequence for the Ring Rolling line to perform maintenance, inspection, lubricant service, and safety verification for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Background and rationale for each major activity are included to support maintenance decisions and records.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before Step 1)
1.1. Production supervisor has authorized the shutdown and issued the work order.  
1.2. All in-process work has been secured and material staged per production hold procedures.  
1.3. Lockout/tagout kits and isolation plans are available and match the equipment IDs listed above.  
1.4. Required spare parts and consumables are staged: lubricants, seals, and filters as specified in maintenance master files. Note the lubricant part numbers: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463. Verify part numbers match order and receipt documentation before use.  
1.5. Notify maintenance, operations, and safety teams via the normal communications channel. Reference ECN-2026-044 for any configuration changes that affect the shutdown scope.

Required PPE (apply to all steps that involve equipment access or energized systems)
1. Hard hat, safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, steel-toe footwear, leather gloves rated for industrial use.  
2. Arc-rated clothing only if hot work or electrical troubleshooting is authorized by the electrical permit.  
3. Respiratory protection when entering confined spaces or when dust levels exceed routine work exposure per facility monitoring. Use SB-1015 for shot-blast specific respiratory controls.

Shutdown sequence and activities (numbered steps)
2. Lockout/Tagout and isolation
2.1. Coordinate with operations to isolate energy sources for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03 following lockout/tagout procedures in MM-P3-L2-SB01. Explain rationale: full isolation prevents accidental startup during inspection and lubricant service.  
2.2. Verify zero energy state with qualified personnel. Record verifier names and time in the shutdown log.

3. External inspection and documentation
3.1. Visually inspect external guards, access panels, and cabling for damage or wear; document findings on the shutdown checklist. Rationale: early detection reduces repair scope and downtime. Example: note frayed cable insulation or missing fasteners and tag components for repair.  
3.2. Update the equipment condition entry in the maintenance management system and attach photographs where possible.

4. Lubricant service and reservoir work
4.1. For EQ-P3-L2-RR02, drain, filter, and refill lubricant reservoirs using only the lubricant identified by the procurement and inventory records. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930. Rationale: correct lubricant viscosity and additive package are critical for bearing life and ring form accuracy. Record batch or lot number of the lubricant used on the service form.  
4.2. For EQ-P3-L2-SB01, perform any required chamber or capture-system lubrication using the approved product. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463. Rationale: shot-blast cabinets require lubricants compatible with abrasive media to avoid media contamination. Record quantity used and supplier lot number.

5. Mechanical inspections and corrective actions
5.1. Inspect bearings, couplings, and drive components per the maintenance checklist. Document any axial or radial play observed and list recommended actions. Rationale: uncontrolled play can affect ring geometry and cause catastrophic failure.  
5.2. Replace worn seals and filters; ensure disposal and replacement are documented per environmental procedures.

6. Hydraulic and pneumatic systems
6.1. Depressurize systems, inspect hoses and fittings for leaks, and replace components as required. Record serials or identifiers of replaced components in the work order.

7. Electrical systems and controls
7.1. With electrical lockout in place, perform inspections of motor terminals, control panels, and cable entries. Note any corrosion, loose terminations, or water ingress and record actions taken. Reference MM-P3-L2-SB01 for panel-level verification points.

8. Functional checks and leak test
8.1. After repairs and fluid fills, restore energy under controlled conditions with one qualified operator at the main panel and one safety observer at the equipment. Rationale: staged re-energization allows immediate response to anomalies. Document results, noting any abnormal noises, leaks, or control alarms.  
8.2. If alarms or unexpected behavior occur, return to lockout and troubleshoot. Attach findings to the maintenance record.

9. Housekeeping and component marking
9.1. Clean work areas, remove tools, and verify all guards and covers are reinstalled. Rationale: residual tools or debris increase incident risk.  
9.2. Mark replaced components with tag identifiers linked to the maintenance record.

Records to keep
10. Shutdown log with verifier signatures and times.  
11. Service forms showing lubricant part numbers and batch/lot numbers used. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463.  
12. Photos of before-and-after conditions.  
13. Completed checklist and follow-up corrective action items entered into the maintenance management system and cross-referenced to the work order. Reference ECN-2026-044 for configuration changes and MM-P3-L2-SB01 for maintenance detail records.

Examples and rationale
13.1. Example entry: “Reservoir drained, visual contamination found, filter replaced, refilled with CFW-LUB-930, batch A123, no abnormal vibration; returned to service.” Rationale: concise entries expedite root-cause analysis if failures recur.  
13.2. Example nonconformance: “Shot-blast cabinet seal worn; lubricant contamination suspected; replaced seal, cleaned cabinet, refilled with CFW-LUB-463.” Provide corrective action and monitor for recurrence.

Sign-off
14. Final verification and acceptance
14.1. Maintenance lead, operations lead, and safety officer must sign the shutdown completion section of the work order, confirming that preconditions are met, inspections completed, and functional tests passed.  
14.2. Attach all records, photos, and parts receipts to the work order and file per document control. Reference SB-1015 for shot-blast safety verification requirements.

Appendix and references
15. Referenced documents: ECN-2026-044, MM-P3-L2-SB01, SB-1015 for supplemental procedures, change records, and safety criteria.
